prompt: How does the lesson describe BABOK's relationship to an order of work?

choices.text: It prescribes six phases done in sequence
choices.why: The knowledge areas are areas of work, not phases; they overlap and repeat.

choices.text: It describes tasks and techniques and lets the analyst choose
choices.why: Right: a vocabulary and a checklist, not a recipe.

choices.text: It is a software tool for managing requirements
choices.why: It is a published guide; tools exist, and none is BABOK.

choices.text: It replaces Scrum on analysis tasks
choices.why: It works alongside any delivery method, including agile ones.

prompt: Finance asks to automate the reconciliation. What is the analyst's first job, by the lesson?

choices.text: Choose the tool that will run the automation
choices.why: That jumps to a solution before the need is understood.

choices.text: Estimate how long the automation will take
choices.why: Estimating a solution nobody has examined is premature.

choices.text: Write the user stories for the job
choices.why: Stories describe a solution; the need comes first.

choices.text: Find the need under the requested solution
choices.why: Yes: automate is a solution; the need is closing the month without two days of manual matching.

prompt: Match each BACCM concept to the reconciliation example.

pairs.right: two days a month to close, and errors reaching the auditors
a daily job matching settlement files with payments
two days a month back for Finance
the gateway's file format and cash refunds at counters

right_distractors: the sprint in which the job is built

prompt: Filling in the six concepts before the workshop, which one was emptiest for the reconciliation, and what did asking about it reveal?

choices.text: Value: the change's worth was unknown
choices.why: Value was clear, two days a month; the gap was elsewhere.

choices.text: Context: agents refund cash, and the gateway never sees it
choices.why: Right: that fact changed the solution, and the model made the question obvious.

choices.text: Stakeholder: the finance director had not been told
choices.why: The director approved the change; the missing stakeholders were found later.

choices.text: Need: the problem was not real
choices.why: The need was real; two days a month is measurable.

prompt: Match each knowledge area to a piece of the reconciliation work.
hint: Planning, asking, managing, strategy, design, evaluation.

pairs.right: a morning watching Joana match files
ids, MoSCoW and who signs off
today's manual process and the target daily match
checking, three months later, whether the month closes in a day

prompt: Which knowledge area does the lesson call the forgotten one?

choices.text: Business Analysis Planning and Monitoring
choices.why: Planning is rarely skipped entirely; going back to check value is.

choices.text: Solution Evaluation
choices.why: Yes: asking whether the value arrived, after the solution is in use.

choices.text: Elicitation and Collaboration
choices.why: Every project elicits something; the question is how well.

choices.text: Requirements Analysis and Design Definition
choices.why: It is where requirements become design, and teams do it, sometimes too soon.

prompt: The station agents have low influence over the project. Where are they on the map, and what does that mean?
hint: The quadrant says how to engage.

choices.text: Monitor: they can be left out of the analysis
choices.why: Their interest is high, and they hold a requirement nobody else knew.

choices.text: Manage closely: they decide the change
choices.why: They do not decide; the finance director does.

choices.text: Keep informed, and visit them at the counter
choices.why: Right: high interest, low influence; they will not come to the workshop.

choices.text: Keep satisfied: they could block it
choices.why: That quadrant is high influence, low interest.

prompt: In a RACI table, each decision has exactly one person marked ___, the one answerable for the outcome.
Which stakeholders were missing from the first reconciliation meeting? Choose all that apply.
hint: One refunds cash; one would be paged at night.

choices.text: The station agents
choices.why: Yes: found by asking what causes the mismatches Joana cannot explain.

choices.text: Platform
choices.why: Yes: they will run the job and be paged when it fails.

choices.text: Joana
choices.why: She does the work today; she was the first person asked.

choices.text: The finance director
choices.why: The director requested and approves the change.

prompt: The interview with Joana took an hour and missed three things. What found them?
hint: People are poor witnesses of their own routines.

choices.text: A survey of the finance department
choices.why: A survey only answers the questions you thought to ask.

choices.text: A morning of observation
choices.why: Right: the refund pass, the exceptions spreadsheet and the phone calls to stations.

choices.text: A workshop with Payments
choices.why: Payments did not know how Joana matched the files.

choices.text: Reading the gateway's documentation
choices.why: Documentation could explain the file, not Joana's routine around it.

prompt: Match each elicitation technique to its blind spot.
hint: Each one sees something the others miss.

pairs.right: people describe what they think they do
the loudest voice wins unless facilitated
people react to the look, not the behaviour

prompt: Tainá sent Joana a summary ending with: what did I get wrong? What would have happened without that step?

choices.text: Every refund would have been reported as a mismatch
choices.why: Yes: the refund settles two days later, not one, and a wrong day breaks every refund match.

choices.text: The finance director would not have approved the change
choices.why: The correction was about a fact, not about approval.

choices.text: Joana would have felt left out
choices.why: Possibly, but the lesson's point is the wrong requirement it prevented.

choices.text: The gateway's file format would have changed
choices.why: That is context, announced by the gateway; confirming had nothing to do with it.

prompt: Match each reconciliation requirement to its BABOK class.
hint: Goals, needs, capabilities, and what exists only for the move.

pairs.left: Finance closes within one working day
Joana sees every unmatched transaction with its reason
the job matches refunds by original id
the 214 known exceptions are imported before the first run

prompt: Why does the lesson say transition requirements are the ones forgotten?
hint: What happens to them after go-live?

choices.text: Because BABOK added them in a recent edition
choices.why: They are part of the classification in the guide; the problem is attention.

choices.text: Because they are non-functional by definition
choices.why: Importing exceptions or running in parallel are neither functional nor quality requirements of the solution.

choices.text: Because the business owner writes them
choices.why: Anybody may write them; the point is that nobody thinks to.

choices.text: They vanish once the move is done
choices.why: Right: they are capabilities of the transition, not of the system, and each can sink the first day.

prompt: Put the MoSCoW categories in order from highest to lowest priority.
trap: Won't is a decision, not a deletion: it stays written down.

prompt: Why is the Won't-have category the important one, by the lesson?
hint: Lesson 5 said the same about rejected options.

choices.text: Writing it down turns an omission into a decision
choices.why: Right: somebody can question it, and nobody rediscovers it as new.

choices.text: It is where the cheapest requirements go
choices.why: Cost is not what puts something in Won't; agreement about scope is.

choices.text: It is the largest category in a healthy project
choices.why: Size is not the point; its existence is.

choices.text: Because those requirements are deleted afterwards
choices.why: The opposite: they are kept, written down, for later.

prompt: A plan has 50 days of effort. By the DSDM rule quoted in the lesson, about how many days at most should the Musts take?
A requirement reads: the job reads the settlement file from an SFTP folder at 03:00 every night. What is the architect's question back?

choices.text: Why SFTP and not an API?
choices.why: That argues about the design inside a requirement; the requirement should not have the design at all.

choices.text: Who will maintain the SFTP server?
choices.why: A good operational question, and it still accepts the design as the requirement.

choices.text: What is the need behind it?
choices.why: Right: the requirement has decided the architecture; the need is when Finance must see the matches.

choices.text: Can it run at 02:00 instead?
choices.why: Moving the time keeps the hidden design.

prompt: How did the requirement complete by 07:00 on a São João day come to be written?

choices.text: The finance director set it in the business case
choices.why: The business case had no number; that was the gap.

choices.text: The gateway's contract required it
choices.why: The gateway says nothing about Carcará's internal job.

choices.text: Platform chose it to match their maintenance window
choices.why: The number came from the business, through a question.

choices.text: Tainá asked when Joana starts work
choices.why: Yes: neither side owned the number until somebody asked.

prompt: With no analyst on the team, what minimum does the lesson suggest the architect borrows from BABOK? Choose all that apply.
hint: One page of concepts, people, one observation, four classes, scope.

choices.text: The six core concepts on one page
choices.why: Yes: the empty headings are the agenda.

choices.text: At least one observation, not only interviews
choices.why: Yes: routines are invisible to the people who do them.

choices.text: The four classes, so transition requirements are not forgotten
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: A CBAP certification before starting
choices.why: The lesson does not prepare for, or require, certification.
